Order intake lessons:
- Forms are version 1 with six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Every observed submission was rejected; failures ranged from 1–3 invalid fields. Do not assume a field is valid based on repeated values.
- Source text is often truncated or noisy (voicemail, phone transcription, handwritten transcription, portal/email). Extract and verify each field carefully rather than relying on the partial JSON shown.
- Customer/email/date combinations observed:
  - Eli Reyes / user559@example.com / 2026-01-03
  - Ada Sato / user683@example.com / 2026-08-28
  - Dee Reyes / user603@example.com / 2026-10-19
  - Bo Sato / user598@example.com / 2026-09-24
  These are observations only, not proof of validity.
- Each order has three attempts. Repeated rejection of the same record does not indicate which fields failed; avoid blindly resubmitting unchanged data.
- After attempt 3, stop and expect manual review; do not spend further attempts on that record.
- Front-desk forwarding notes and duplicate-check claims are context, not validation evidence.

Order intake lessons:
- Form version 1 has six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Verify every field from the complete source; voicemail, phone, handwriting, portal, and pasted email text may be truncated or noisy. Never rely on partial JSON or repeated values.
- Every field tuple is untrusted until accepted. Repeated rejection does not identify the invalid fields, and repeated forwarding/confirmation or duplicate-check claims are not validation.
- Confirmed accepted tuple: Bo Sato / user598@example.com / 2026-09-24 (ORD-5111, attempt 3). The same apparent tuple was rejected earlier (ORD-5110, 2 invalid), so prior rejection does not prove the tuple is permanently wrong; investigate source extraction and all six fields before retrying.
- Observed but unvalidated tuples:
  - Eli Reyes / user559@example.com / 2026-01-03
  - Ada Sato / user683@example.com / 2026-08-28
  - Dee Reyes / user603@example.com / 2026-10-19
  - Ada Sato / user119@example.com / 2026-04-14
  - Cy Marsh / user104@example.com / 2026-09-15
  - Bo Reyes / user786@example.com / 2026-12-23
- Ada’s alternate tuple was rejected twice (2 invalid, then 2 invalid); Cy’s tuple was rejected three times, including identical 2-field failures; Bo Reyes was rejected twice with 2 invalid fields. These patterns still do not reveal which fields failed.
- Each order has three attempts. After attempt 3, stop; send to manual review and do not resubmit unchanged data.
